recognize_zh: 薄片中受感染的紅血球明顯比周圍紅血球大、顏色偏淡，並布滿細小粉紅色 Schüffner 點，胞內有不規則的阿米巴狀滋養體與少量棕色色素；這組合指向間日瘧（Plasmodium vivax）。
features: Three infected red cells enlarged (about 1.5 times normal) and paler than uninfected cells
Fine, uniform pink-red Schüffner's stippling throughout the infected red cells
Irregular amoeboid trophozoites with red chromatin dots, elongated or fragmented blue cytoplasm and small golden-brown pigment granules
No multiply infected cells, appliqué forms or crescent gametocytes
Uninfected red cells normocytic and normochromic; scattered platelets in the background
describe_en: Leishman-stained thin blood film shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with three infected erythrocytes. Infected cells are enlarged and paler than neighboring red cells and contain fine pink Schüffner's stippling, with irregular amoeboid trophozoites bearing red chromatin dots, elongated blue cytoplasm and scant golden-brown pigment. No multiply infected cells, appliqué forms or crescentic gametocytes are seen. Scattered platelets are present and should not be mistaken for extracellular parasites. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax trophozoites.

ddx.vs: Falciparum infects normal-sized red cells without Schüffner's dots and shows delicate rings, multiple infections, appliqué forms and banana-shaped gametocytes.
Ovale also enlarges and stipples red cells, but infected cells are oval with fimbriated edges and trophozoites are compact rather than amoeboid.
Malariae-infected red cells are normal or small without stippling, with band-form trophozoites and coarse dark pigment.
Babesia forms small pleomorphic rings, sometimes tetrads, without pigment, stippling or red cell enlargement.
